key_insight: The paper builds a benchmark framework that maps realistic nuclear many-body Hamiltonians to qubit form so quantum eigensolvers can be compared on consistent, physics-grounded problems.
engineering_relevance: It gives quantum algorithm developers concrete resource estimates for nuclear simulations, helping choose between QPE, Quantum Krylov, and ODMD under different model spaces and interaction sets.
method: Map chiral EFT nuclear interactions from second quantization to qubit Hamiltonians.
Construct benchmark instances for no-core and valence-space nuclear problems with NN and selected 3N terms.
Estimate T-gate and system-size costs for QPE, Quantum Krylov, and ODMD using Trotterization, qubitization, and QSVT primitives.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates scaling trends via resource estimates rather than experimental runs, comparing T-gate counts and system size across benchmark classes and algorithms.
watch_item: Resource estimates depend on the chosen model-space formulation and included interactions, so direct comparisons require careful, consistent benchmark definitions.
paper_title: Nuclear Many-Body Systems as Benchmarks for Quantum Computing
